notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Round any monetary Decimal result with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Signal domain failures by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with a stable snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` or `negative_amount`, and include the offending value via `repr`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 require approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given; amounts at or below 500.00 need none.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Use to_money and ZERO from ledgerly.money: Normalize line prices with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Reject bools when validating integers: When validating an integer argument, explicitly exclude `bool` (e.g. `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int)`) because `True`/`False` are ints in Python and would otherwise pass.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: Use `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` to normalize any datetime input (e.g. `after`, `sub.started_at`) before comparing or doing arithmetic, so naive and aware datetimes are handled consistently.
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
